feature: Updates are offered only once they can be downloaded
summary: Check for Updates no longer offers a version the website names before its download exists; it says you are up to date until the download answers. If a download is still refused, the message says the update isn't ready yet instead of a server error.
setup: Installed Photonz (release build), no flag changed. The answers below were measured on the probe against the real website and GitHub downloads with --update-check-diag (docs/design/release.md).

try.do: On Photonz 0.21.0, choose Check for Updates. Measured: up to date.
On an older build (measured as 0.20.0), choose Check for Updates. Measured: offers 0.21.0.
Next release: while the website already names it but the release page has no DMG yet, choose Check for Updates. Measured with a stub naming 0.99.0: up to date.
Once the DMG is published, choose Check for Updates again. Measured: offers it.
If Update & Restart is refused by the download server, read the alert. Measured on v0.99.0: "This update isn't ready to download yet. Try again in a few minutes."

evaluate: Is "up to date" the right thing to say while a release is half out, rather than "an update is coming"?
Does the not-ready message read plainly enough under the "Couldn't install the update" title?
rough: No picture: the outcome is a system alert driven by the live servers, which no walk opens, so this was measured with the probe's --update-check-diag and its text output instead.

While a release is half out, someone two versions behind is told they are up to date for those minutes even though the previous release is downloadable; the next check (every six hours, or by hand) offers the new one.
